column1: # selfbuilt.tsv — images this repo BUILDS FROM SOURCE because no free published build exists.
# WHY THIS FILE IS SEPARATE FROM images/images.txt. images.txt is a MIRROR inventory: every row is
# pulled from a public registry and pushed to Harbor. A row here has no upstream image to pull — we
# build it on the internet box and carry the result. Putting one in images.txt would make
# `make mirror-pull` try to pull a tag that does not exist.
# WHY NOT apps/registry.tsv. That registry is per-APP: 41 files consume app_names/for_each_app, and
# every row implies a deploy dir, a Gitea repo pair, an ArgoCD Application, an ingress host and a
# `make verify` marker assertion. An infra image has none of those. (MEASURED 2026-08-26:
# `grep -rln 'app_names\|for_each_app' scripts/ Makefile` -> 41. An earlier draft said 40, taken before
# 14-selfbuilt-build.sh existed and mentioned app_names in its own header.)
# REPRODUCIBILITY. The pin is the upstream GIT REF, and the anchor recorded after a build is the
# RESULTING DIGEST. "Build from the default branch" is disqualifying for an air gap: two operators
# cutting a bundle a day apart would carry different binaries under the same name, and the digest in
# images.lock would stop meaning anything.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   name      short id, used for the bundle tarball name
#   git_url   upstream source
#   git_ref   an IMMUTABLE tag — never a branch
#   dockerfile  path within the checkout
#   target      docker build --target (empty = default stage)
#   repo_path   path under ${HARBOR_URL}/${HARBOR_INFRA_PROJECT}/
#   tag         the tag the consuming manifest asks for.
#               ⚠️ IT MUST ENCODE ANY go_get OVERRIDE, NOT JUST THE UPSTREAM REF. Our artifact is
#               "fork v1.25.18 PLUS go-containerregistry v0.21.9" -- tagging that as plain
#               `v1.25.18-debug` misrepresents its content, and it is not merely cosmetic: MEASURED
#               2026-08-26, pushing different content under an already-cached tag left the KinD nodes
#               running the OLD binary (Tekton steps are imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent), so a verified
#               fix appeared not to work and cost a full e2e cycle. Same mutable-tag class the repo's
#               Harbor blob-store incident is about: the digest in selfbuilt.lock is the truth, the
#               tag is only a label -- so make the label change whenever the content does.
#   go_get      OPTIONAL, space-separated module@version overrides applied BEFORE the build
# WHY go_get EXISTS — and it is the single strongest argument for building rather than mirroring.
# MEASURED 2026-08-26 on a live pipeline: fork v1.25.18 pins go-containerregistry v0.21.5, which
# carries an SSRF guard that REFUSES a bearer-token realm whose host is a private/RFC1918 address:
#     creating push check transport for 172.18.0.3 failed: invalid realm in www-authenticate:
#     realm host "172.18.0.3" is a private or link-local address
# ⚠️ SCOPE — CORRECTED 2026-08-26, and the first version of this line OVERSTATED it. The guard keys
# on `net.ParseIP(host) != nil`, so it fires only when the realm host is an IP LITERAL. Measured
# both ways: our KinD Harbor is addressed as 172.18.0.3 and echoes realm="https://172.18.0.3/..."
# -> the guard FIRES. The VKS lab addresses Harbor as harbor.env1.lab.test and echoes
# realm="https://harbor.env1.lab.test/..." -> NOT an IP -> the guard does NOT fire. So this breaks
# an IP-ADDRESSED Harbor, not "every air-gapped Harbor". It still blocks our own e2e gate, which is
# reason enough -- and an FQDN is a deployment choice a consumer may not make. Upstream
# added an exemption for "realm matching the registry host:port" on 2026-05-18 (bf87c3bf, #2302),
# first released in v0.21.6 -- `git compare v0.21.5...bf87c3bf` reports ahead_by=30, i.e. the fork
# ships the guard WITHOUT its fix. Bumping the dependency is only possible because we BUILD; a
# mirrored published image offers no such lever.
# Proven behaviourally, both binaries against the real Harbor: v1.24.0 pushes, v1.25.18-as-shipped
# FAILS, v1.25.18 rebuilt with v0.21.9 PUSHES.
# ⚠️ WHY v0.21.9 AND NOT THE "MINIMUM" v0.21.6 — DO NOT MINIMISE THIS PIN.
# v0.21.6 is the first release carrying the realm exemption, so it LOOKS like the smallest safe
# bump, and an adversary round argued exactly that (51 fewer commits through kaniko's hot path).
# It was tried, and MEASURED 2026-08-27: kaniko built with v0.21.6 dies at the FIRST layer pull:
#   INFO Unpacking rootfs as cmd COPY .mvn/ .mvn/ requires it.
#   fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!
#   go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/remote.(*pullLimiter).acquire  .../remote/limiter.go:37
# The fix is IN the v0.21.6..v0.21.9 range: ggcr #2373 "remote: release pull limiter slot when body
# is read to EOF" (limiter.go +8/-0, limiter_test.go +54/-0). So the two things we need land in
# DIFFERENT releases -- the exemption in v0.21.6, the limiter fix after it -- and v0.21.9 is the
# first version that has both. "Smallest blast radius" is the wrong axis here: the commits being
# skipped contain a fix this build REQUIRES.
# The override cannot be avoided either: there is NO env/flag alternative (zero os.Getenv in either
# transport tree; --insecure gates only the SCHEME), upstream issue #2258 asked for a disable option
# that was never implemented, and bumping the fork does not help -- v1.25.19 (2026-08-27) still pins
# ⚠️ THE FORK VENDORS ITS DEPENDENCIES. `go get` alone leaves vendor/ stale and the build dies with
# `go: inconsistent vendoring` at the credential-helper step -- an error naming neither the module
# nor the override. The producer therefore runs `go mod vendor` after any go_get. And do NOT run
# `go mod tidy`: it PRUNES the tool dependency that deploy/Dockerfile installs, which fails the same
# step for a completely different reason.
# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=chainguard-forks/kaniko
kaniko
